title: Make Django settings environment-driven
description: Scaffold settings hardcode SECRET_KEY, DEBUG=True, ALLOWED_HOSTS=[] and sqlite. Production deploy is impossible until settings read from env. Add django-environ, .env.sample, Postgres via DATABASE_URL, and wire DRF/CORS/spectacular into INSTALLED_APPS (DRF is installed but unregistered).
acceptance_criteria: No secrets in source; DEBUG defaults False; DATABASE_URL drives Postgres; .env.sample documents every var

title: Record which items are worth chasing (meeting Q2)
description:
Carries the answer to Question 2 of the stakeholder discussion guide: which items warrant a follow-up scan (returned or recorded as used) and which are simply consumed at check-out.

Seeded guess from price and observed return rate, for correction by users:
  chase it   UAP-AC-IW (6% returned), LiteBeam (23%), OmniTikPOE (63%), SXTsq US (68%), WiFi6-ONT (64%)
  unsure     ToughCable (57%), Indoor Cat 6 (23%), Tp-Link (39%), RJ45 ToughCable connectors (44%)
  used up    RJ45 passthrough (95%), RJ-45 Coupler Indoors (53%), Zip Ties (84%)

Cable is the one most needing a human: 68% of ToughCable check-ins are partial amounts (1453, 304, 225), which looks like people returning half-used boxes - so treating it as consumed would lose real information. That rests on only 22 check-ins.

Becomes a per-item field plus seed data.
acceptance_criteria: Every catalogued item has an explicit answer, recorded as data rather than prose, and the ones nobody could decide are marked as such rather than silently defaulted.

title: Record the real list of stock locations (meeting Q5)
description:
Carries the answer to Question 5 of the stakeholder discussion guide: where stock is actually kept.

The old sheet had no location concept, so people wrote them into the notes field. Observed: 'Sean mesh room 131 broome st' (175 rows), 'apartment stock', 'backup shelf', 'incoming package shelf', 'Set aside for SN1', 'Moving inventory to basement', plus references to SN1, SN3, Grand St, Olmsted, Mil Mundos, Greenwood Cemetery.

Needs the real list from people who use the space: rooms, shelves, hubs, supernodes. Locations nest (site -> room -> shelf), so rough input is fine.

Also settle whether 'in a volunteer's flat' is a location, which is the same decision as inventory-tng-8sq wearing a different hat.
acceptance_criteria: Seed data exists for the locations that matter, so the system is usable on day one without each volunteer inventing names.

title: OWNER DECISION: how is the inventory app itself authorised
acceptance_criteria: The project owner has chosen a posture; the permission classes on the write endpoints match it; docs/deployment.md and the architecture 'Not yet built' authentication bullet are updated.

title: Cart state: context, reducer, localStorage persistence
description:
Decision 0011 section 13. The cart is shared by the scanner, the item list, the volunteer picker and the submit bar. One useReducer behind a React context, no state management library.

Two behaviours belong to the reducer, not the UI:
- scanning the same label twice increments an existing line, it does not add a second one;
- a scan is debounced, because a camera decodes the same code many times a second and every decode would otherwise be a quantity increment.

Persist to localStorage on every dispatch: a phone that locks or reloads must not lose 24 scans. The idempotency key is minted when the cart is CREATED, not at submit, so every retry of the same cart carries the same key.
acceptance_criteria: Cart survives a reload; duplicate scans increment rather than duplicate; debounce is tested; idempotency key is stable across the cart's life.

title: Item list screen: search, steppers and quantity chips
description:
The volunteer's own mockup, and the path that works with no camera and no readable label: every item with its current count, and a way to add it to the cart.

The mockup's bare -1/[n]/+1 stepper is not enough on its own for an item stocked in the hundreds. The distinct quantities on an item's active labels ARE that item's packaging, so offer them as one-tap chips (+1 and +100 (packet) side by side).

The resulting quantity is always shown spelled out in the item's own unit - 'Zip Ties Reusable - 100 each (1 packet)' - and is editable in one tap. Nothing is ever added silently: that visibility is what closes the packet ambiguity (decision 0011 section 6).
acceptance_criteria: Items and balances render; search works; adding via stepper or chip puts a line in the cart with a visible, editable quantity; queried by role and accessible name in tests.

title: Volunteer picker with search-first self-registration
description: Every batch needs an actor. The picker searches existing volunteers before offering to create one, and the device remembers the choice so nobody retypes their name on every submission - which is what produced 102 spellings of 65 people in the sheet.
acceptance_criteria: Search shows near-matches before the create option; choice persists on the device; a newly self-registered volunteer can immediately be the actor on a batch.

title: Scanner: camera via BarcodeDetector ponyfill, plus wedge and manual code entry
description:
Decision 0011 sections 2 and 3.

Camera: use the barcode-detector ponyfill over zxing-wasm, programmed against the BarcodeDetector interface so there is one code path. Native BarcodeDetector is absent on Chrome/Linux and Chrome/Windows, off by default in Safari, and absent in Firefox, so WASM is the primary decoder rather than a fallback. Three non-optional constraints: self-host the .wasm asset (no CDN - the page has to work in a basement and the frontend image is self-contained), dynamic-import it so the list-and-stepper user never downloads a megabyte, and offer a camera picker from enumerateDevices() because iOS has a documented history of answering facingMode:environment with the ultra-wide lens.

Wedge/manual: one focused text input that submits on Enter and clears itself. Costs nearly nothing, supports USB/Bluetooth scanner guns with no browser API, and is the escape hatch for typing the code printed under a dead QR.

Confirm the camera confirms audibly - a Web Audio beep plus navigator.vibrate where it exists. The volunteer is looking at the shelf, not the screen.
acceptance_criteria: Scanning adds a resolved line to the cart on desktop Firefox/Chrome-Linux and on a phone; the wasm asset is served from our own origin; the decoder is not in the initial bundle; a wedge scanner and a typed code both work; an unknown code offers item search rather than dead-ending.

title: Submit the batch: retry, per-line errors and warnings
description:
One Save button, as in the mockup. Posts the whole cart to POST /api/stock/transactions.

A failed Save leaves the cart intact and offers Retry - safe because the idempotency key is stable. A 400 highlights the offending cart lines in place using the index in each error, rather than showing a wall of text. A 200 (already posted) is treated as success.

Warnings, including negative balance, are shown without blocking or nagging: a negative balance is a prompt to run a stock count, and an interface that treats it as an error sends volunteers back to inventing corrections.
acceptance_criteria: Successful submit clears the cart; a network failure keeps it and Retry does not double-post; per-line errors are shown against the right lines; warnings render as advice, not as failure.

title: Label resolve endpoint: GET /api/labels/{code} and the cached snapshot
description:
Decision 0011 section 8. Resolves a scanned or typed code to what it points at.

Response carries code, kind (item|location), quantity, revoked_at, and whichever of item/location is populated. Unknown code -> 404 with a typed error body. Revoked label -> 200 with revoked_at set, because a retired sticker still says what it pointed at and refusing the scan would block a volunteer over bookkeeping.

Lookup normalises first: uppercase, and fold Crockford-ambiguous characters (I and L to 1, O to 0) so a code typed off a faded label resolves.

Also GET /api/labels, the whole active set, so the client can cache it and resolve scans with no network round trip in a basement (decision 0011 section 12).
acceptance_criteria: Both endpoints return typed bodies including the 404; ambiguous-character folding is tested; revoked labels resolve rather than 404; openapi.yaml regenerated.

title: Batch endpoint: POST /api/stock/transactions
description:
The endpoint this project exists for. Decision 0011 section 8-11.

One request creates one StockTransaction and one StockMovement per line, inside one database transaction. Movements reference items by id, not by label code.

- 201 created; 200 when the idempotency_key was already posted (return the transaction created the first time); 400 nothing saved; 409 internally inconsistent batch.
- Idempotency matched on the key ALONE, no request-body hash. Same key twice returns the first transaction.
- All-or-nothing, but validation must not stop at the first failure: the 400 body lists every rejected line with its index in the submitted movements array, so the volunteer fixes everything in one pass.
- A movement that drives a balance negative is RECORDED and reported in a warnings array, never rejected. Refusing it is the mistake the sheet makes and is why 18.7% of the existing ledger is faked corrections.

Uses the project default permission class for now; see the authorisation decision bead.
acceptance_criteria: Batch posts atomically; replayed idempotency key returns 200 and creates nothing; a batch with three bad lines returns all three by index and writes nothing; negative balance produces a warning and a recorded movement; 200/201/400/409 all document typed bodies; openapi.yaml regenerated.
close_reason: POST /api/stock/transactions with 201/200/400/409, per-line error indices, negative-balance warnings and idempotency recovery; ADR 0011 amended to record the 409

title: Catalogue read endpoints: items with balances, locations, categories
description:
The item list is the primary UI in decision 0011 (and the whole of the volunteer mockup), so it needs an endpoint before anything else can be built. GET /api/items must carry current balance per location from the StockBalance view, the unit of measure, and the item's active labels with their quantities (those are what the UI offers as one-tap quantity chips). Plus GET /api/locations and GET /api/categories.

Filtering via django-filter, not ad-hoc query parsing. Add each to the ENDPOINTS index in inventory/views.py.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoints serve items+balances, locations and categories; every operation documents a typed response body; backend/openapi.yaml regenerated in the same change; tests go through the API.

title: Volunteer endpoints: search-first list and self-registration
description:
Volunteers are a pick-list with no password (decision 0008 point 5). The UI must search existing volunteers before offering to create one - that trigram search is what prevents a second generation of 102 spellings for 65 people.

GET /api/volunteers with a fuzzy name search using the existing pg_trgm GIN index, and POST /api/volunteers to self-register. Merged volunteers (merged_into set) must not appear as choices.
acceptance_criteria: Search returns near-matches by similarity; self-registration works; merged and inactive volunteers are excluded from the pick-list; typed response bodies; openapi.yaml regenerated; tests through the API.

title: Add Label.quantity: what one scan of a label means
description:
Decision 0011 section 6. A label goes on a packet, and nothing in the model says what one scanned label means. The sheet shows zip ties recorded as both 1 (one packet) and 100 (a packet of ties) by different volunteers, so roughly a third of those rows are wrong by 100x.

Add Label.quantity: DecimalField(max_digits=12, decimal_places=3, default=1) with a check constraint requiring > 0. Meaning: scanning this token means this much of this item. Lets a box-of-305m label and a shelf-of-offcuts label be two labels on one item.
acceptance_criteria: Field, migration and check constraint in place; docs/data-model.md Label section updated in the same change (docs change with the code); tests cover the constraint.
close_reason: Label.quantity, positive and location-pinned check constraints, migration, tests and data-model.md update landed

title: Require type annotations on all Python code
description:
Python typing is optional; TypeScript's is not. ty was already in CI but a type CHECKER does not require annotations - it checks what is there and infers the rest, so a file with zero annotations passed clean. Nothing was asking for types.

Requirement from Ali: types are REQUIRED, but need NOT be perfect or maximally specific, because the project wants volunteer participation. Docs must state the requirement and link to Python typing references, and there must be deterministic machinery so IDEs and coding agents can get help defining types.
acceptance_criteria: ruff ANN rules enforced via the existing ruff check step; Any permitted (ANN401 off); requirement documented at DEVELOPERS.md#typing with learning links; deterministic helper commands documented; ADR recorded.
close_reason: Implemented and verified. ruff ANN enabled in backend/pyproject.toml so the existing 'ruff check' step enforces it in CI with no new tool or command; ANN401 off so Any is a legal annotation and there is always a way through. Generated migrations exempt. Documented at DEVELOPERS.md#typing (bar, three helper commands, ty's blind spots, editor setup, learning links), Definition of Done, AGENTS.md, and the django-backend skill. ADR docs/decisions/0009-type-annotations-required.md. Verified both directions: unannotated code fails, Any passes.

title: Implement catalogue models
description:
Implement the reference-data half of docs/data-model.md: Volunteer, Location, Category, Item, ItemIdentifier, Vendor, VendorOffer, Label.

Includes the constraints the model doc specifies rather than leaving them to application code: partial unique indexes on Volunteer.email/slack_id, the held_by <-> volunteer_custody check on Location, and a unique index on the normalised ItemIdentifier value so a scanned or typed string resolves to exactly one item.

django-simple-history goes on these tables (catalogue records need edit history); it does NOT go on the ledger.
acceptance_criteria: Models, migration, and admin registration exist. Constraints are enforced at the database level and covered by tests. Coverage threshold met, ruff/ty pass.
close_reason: Catalogue models implemented: Category, Volunteer, Location, Item, ItemIdentifier, Vendor, VendorOffer, Label, with django-simple-history on all of them and admin registration. All invariants from docs/data-model.md are database constraints, each covered by a test that asserts IntegrityError. 43 tests pass at 100% coverage; ruff, ruff format and ty all clean. Docs updated in the same change: docs/data-model.md (Label design changed during implementation to two nullable FKs plus a check constraint, rather than a generic relation), docs/architecture.md, and the django-backend skill.

title: Implement stock ledger models
description:
Implement StockTransaction and StockMovement per docs/data-model.md, plus the derived balance view.

Key invariants, all as database constraints: at least one of from_location/to_location set; from != to; quantity > 0 (direction is expressed by which side the location sits on, never by sign). Ledger tables get UPDATE/DELETE revoked so append-only is a database guarantee, not a convention - see docs/decisions/0008.

The custody-depth question (inventory-tng-8sq) does NOT block this: the schema is identical under all three options.
acceptance_criteria: Models, migration, balance view, and constraint tests exist. Attempting to update or delete a movement fails. Coverage threshold met.
close_reason: StockTransaction, StockMovement and the derived StockBalance view implemented. All invariants are database constraints (quantity > 0, at least one side, from != to, partial-unique idempotency key). Append-only is enforced by a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger rather than by revoking privileges: verified that the postgres image makes POSTGRES_USER a superuser, and superusers bypass privilege checks, so a REVOKE would have enforced nothing. docs/data-model.md, ADR 0008 and docs/architecture.md corrected to match in the same change. 59 tests pass at 100% coverage; ruff, format and ty clean.

title: Fail CI when the OpenAPI schema is out of date
description:
Requirement from Ali: the backend MUST publish an OpenAPI spec in the current stable format, and it MUST stay in step with the endpoints and payloads.

Documenting that as a rule will not keep it true. Commit the generated schema and add a CI step that regenerates it and fails on any diff, in the same spirit as the coverage and style gates (docs/decisions/0007). drf-spectacular is already a dependency.

Also settle and record: which OpenAPI version drf-spectacular emits and whether that is the current stable release - verify, do not assume. Serve Swagger UI or Redoc for human readers and make the schema endpoint discoverable from the API root.
acceptance_criteria: Schema is committed, CI fails on drift, a human-readable UI is served, and the OpenAPI version choice is recorded in docs/decisions/.
close_reason: OAS_VERSION pinned to 3.1.1 (verified drf-spectacular emits 3.0.3 by default and supports 3.1/3.2; chose 3.1 for JSON Schema 2020-12 alignment with broad tooling support). Schema committed at backend/openapi.yaml. Currency is enforced by a TEST rather than a separate CI step, so local and CI runs are identical - same shape as ADR 0007's coverage gate; verified the test actually fails on drift and passes once regenerated. A second test requires every operation to document a typed response body, which caught that the health endpoint documented no payload at all. Added /api endpoint index for discovery. ADR docs/decisions/0010-openapi-version.md; documented at DEVELOPERS.md#the-api-schema.

title: compose.yaml Postgres volume mount breaks local dev on postgres:18
description:
compose.yaml mounts postgres_data at /var/lib/postgresql/data. The postgres:18 image stores data in major-version-specific subdirectories under /var/lib/postgresql and refuses to start when it finds a mount at the old path:

  Error: in 18+, these Docker images are configured to store database data in a
  format which is compatible with pg_ctlcluster ... there appears to be
  PostgreSQL data in: /var/lib/postgresql/data (unused mount/volume)

The container exits 1, so 'uv run pytest' fails for anyone following DEVELOPERS.md. CI is unaffected because the GitHub Actions service container declares no volume, which is why this was never caught.

Fix: mount the volume at /var/lib/postgresql.
acceptance_criteria: podman/docker compose up -d postgres starts cleanly and 'uv run pytest' passes locally.
close_reason: compose.yaml now mounts postgres_data at /var/lib/postgresql. Verified: container reports healthy and 'uv run pytest' passes (1 passed, 100% coverage). No doc change needed - the documented command is unchanged.

title: MEETING INPUT: six decisions for collaborators and users
description:
Discussion guide published for the stakeholder/user meeting: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/5bf7777e-b392-4eea-90f3-6fcf8fc3bf2c

Reframed after analysing the sheet. The original A/B/C custody question was too coarse: cable behaves like custody, not like a consumable (68% of ToughCable check-ins are partial amounts such as 1453, 304, 225 - people bring back half-used boxes), while zip ties clearly are consumed. So 'how much custody tracking' is not one dial for the system; it is a per-item property.

Q1 custody/consumption (this bead)  - does a volunteer record hardware used at an install? A/B/C.
Q2 which items are worth chasing    - inventory-tng-2zx
Q3 what one scan of a packet means  - settled by ADR 0011 decision 6 (quantity on Label, never implicit)
Q4 pack size vs reorder quantity    - inventory-tng-7na
Q5 real list of locations           - inventory-tng-o5t
Q6 who is allowed to record things  - inventory-tng-0pj

Supporting evidence: 54% of equipment check-outs already carry a note and 13% already name a node, so willingness to record context exists - the current form just has nowhere to put it.
acceptance_criteria: Stakeholders have chosen A, B or C. ADR 0008 status updated from 'proposed' to 'accepted' and its open-question section replaced with the decision.
notes:
Q4 finding, ready to act on once confirmed: the sheet's 'units per order' column means two different things.
  Zip Ties   $12.49 / 100  -> pack size (12.49 buys 100 ties)
  UAP-AC-M   $99.00 / 5    -> reorder quantity (99 EACH, buy 5 at a time)
  ToughCable $163.99 / 305 -> pack size (a 305m box)
  Tp-Link    $30.00 / 10   -> implies $3 a router, which is simply wrong
This is why Item.reorder_quantity and VendorOffer.units_per_order were ambiguous in docs/data-model.md. They are genuinely two different facts and the model already has two fields; the data needs classifying per item.

Caveat for anyone citing the cable finding: it rests on 22 check-ins. It agrees with the free-text notes but is indicative, not conclusive.

title: Enforce test coverage and unify style tooling
description: Add build-breaking coverage gates to backend and frontend, migrate to the Astral toolchain (uv/ruff/ty) and Biome, and document both in DEVELOPERS.md as the single source of truth.
close_reason: Coverage gates enforced at 90% in pytest and vitest; ruff/ty and Biome adopted; documented once in DEVELOPERS.md and referenced everywhere else

title: Configure git remote and beads Dolt sync
description: No git remote exists. Create nycmeshnet/inventory-tng, add origin, then 'bd dolt remote add origin <url>' and 'bd dolt push' so beads issues sync off this machine. Beads warns on every write until this is done.
close_reason: origin added as default upstream and pushed; bd dolt remote configured and pushed to refs/dolt/data

title: DESIGN: QR multi-scan batch transaction flow
description: KEY FEATURE. Current system supports one QR scan per item; the replacement MUST retain QR scanning AND add scanning multiple codes into a single transaction (cart/batch model). Decide browser camera scanning library vs keyboard-wedge hardware scanners; design the batch API.
close_reason: Design complete: docs/decisions/0011-qr-batch-scanning.md. Cart is the interface, scanning is one of three ways to fill it; WASM decoding primary (native BarcodeDetector verified absent on Chrome Windows/Linux and Firefox, off by default in Safari, partial on Chrome macOS); wall QR and item labels unified as one Label mechanism; Label.quantity closes the packet-vs-piece ambiguity. 15 implementation beads created. Two questions left for the owner: app authorisation (inventory-tng-0pj) and what historical zip-tie 1s meant. Went through review, four-lens simplify, and correction: the ADR was cut 552 -> 310 lines and ten factual claims were corrected, including a browser-support table that was wrong and a deployment claim about rejected certificates that was false.

title: DESIGN: inventory data model
description: Model Item/Asset, Location, Category, Transaction/Movement, and audit history. Must cover everything the current Google Sheet (15k+ rows) tracks. Consider django-simple-history for audit trail, as MeshDB uses.
notes:
DESIGN SETTLED 2026-08-18. Model documented in docs/data-model.md; rationale in docs/decisions/0008-stock-ledger-transfer-graph.md.

Decisions taken with Ali:
1. Stock is a double-entry transfer graph (from_location -> to_location), NOT a signed counter. Volunteer custody is a location.
2. Volunteers are a pick-list with no password, self-registration allowed, search-first dedup + admin merge with ledger repointing.
3. All items fungible (quantity-tracked). Serialised Asset table deferred.
4. job_reference is a structured indexed field; no live MeshDB integration.
5. Stock counts are first-class: enter observed quantity, system posts the delta as an adjustment.
6. QR labels carry an opaque token, never a display name.
7. Quantities are Decimal(12,3) with unit_of_measure on Item.
8. Ledger is append-only (UPDATE/DELETE revoked at role level); django-simple-history on catalogue tables only.

OPEN: how much custody tracking to ask volunteers for (options A/B/C in ADR 0008). Schema is identical under all three, so this does NOT block implementation.
close_reason: Design complete and documented: docs/data-model.md (entity model) and docs/decisions/0008-stock-ledger-transfer-graph.md (rationale). All schema decisions settled with Ali. The remaining custody-depth question is a workflow decision tracked separately as inventory-tng-8sq and does not block implementation.

title: Write CONTRIBUTING.md volunteer on-ramp
description: NYC Mesh is a volunteer community; lowering barrier to entry is a primary goal. Clear path from zero to running app to first PR, explicitly usable without AI agents.

title: Write docs/deployment.md
description: Canonical deploy doc covering the shared Dockerfile+Helm artifact set for standard k8s (k3s on Proxmox) and CodeNOW (nycmesh.codenow.com). Env var matrix, migrations, superuser, static files.

title: Add CI workflows and PR/issue templates
description: GitHub Actions: backend lint+test, frontend lint+build, docker build, and a markdown link checker that enforces the doc single-source-of-truth linking. PR template carries the mandatory docs-updated checkbox.

title: Write docs/architecture.md
description: Canonical architecture doc: monorepo rationale, backend/frontend/DB choices, how it mirrors MeshDB and where it deliberately diverges, planned Celery/QR pieces. Single source of truth - all other docs link here.

title: Scaffold Vite + React 19 + MUI frontend
description: frontend/ with Vite, React 19, TypeScript, MUI 9, eslint+prettier, vitest. Builds to static assets served by nginx - no Node runtime in production.

title: Add Helm chart at infra/helm/inventory-tng
description: Single chart deploying backend (gunicorn) + frontend (nginx) + service/ingress/config. Serves BOTH standard k8s and CodeNOW - per docs.codenow.com custom stacks, CodeNOW consumes your own Dockerfile + Helm chart, so there is no second deploy path.

title: Add compose.yaml and devcontainer for local dev
description: Postgres 18 + backend + frontend for one-command local startup. Devcontainer so volunteers can start with zero host setup.

title: Restructure backend to src/ layout mirroring MeshDB
description: Move backend/inventory_tng/{manage.py,inventory_tng,quickstart} to backend/src/{manage.py,inventory_tng,inventory}. Mirrors MeshDB (src/meshdb project pkg + src/meshapi domain app). Drop the empty scaffolded quickstart app.
acceptance_criteria: manage.py check passes from new location; no stale imports

title: Rebuild AGENTS.md as a thin router (<40 lines)
description: Collapse the ~4x duplicated beads content (hand-written preamble + BEADS INTEGRATION block + BEADS CODEX SETUP block + hook-injected bd prime output) into one pointer. Keep only universally-required context: orientation, doc pointers, bd pointer, conservative git policy, non-interactive shell flags, quality gate, skill index. Do not hand-edit inside beads managed markers.

title: Add backend dependency manifest (pyproject.toml + uv.lock)
description: backend/ has a uv-created .venv but no pyproject.toml or requirements.txt, so setup is unreproducible and a Dockerfile has nothing to install from. Pin the four installed packages (django 6.0.5, djangorestframework 3.17.1, asgiref 3.11.1, sqlparse 0.5.5) and requires-python >=3.14.

title: The /api index cannot advertise a write-only endpoint
description:
views.py states the invariant 'an endpoint cannot be advertised without being described, or described without being advertised', and DEVELOPERS.md tells clients to discover the API by fetching /api and following the links. POST /api/stock/transactions -- the endpoint the project exists for -- is in neither, because test_api_root_links_actually_resolve GETs every advertised link and asserts 200, which a POST-only endpoint cannot satisfy.

So the index's contract is really 'GET this and it resolves', not 'here is the API'. Either the index carries a method alongside each link and the test follows suit, or discovery is declared to be the OpenAPI schema's job and the claim in views.py and DEVELOPERS.md is corrected to match. Raised while implementing inventory-tng-hgm.
acceptance_criteria: A client following the documented discovery path can find every endpoint, or the documentation no longer claims they can. views.py's ENDPOINTS comment matches whatever is decided.

title: Enforce TLS at the Helm chart rather than in prose
description:
Raised by the /simplify altitude pass on ADR 0011.

ADR 0011 establishes that TLS is a FUNCTIONAL requirement, not only a security one: without a secure context navigator.mediaDevices is undefined and QR scanning disappears silently. But infra/helm/inventory-tng still exposes ingress.tls.enabled as a toggle, templates/ingress.yaml simply branches on it, and there is no values.schema.json. So the only thing between an operator and a scanner-less install is a paragraph in docs/deployment.md.

The repo's own pattern is to enforce invariants where the mistake is made rather than describe them where they might be read. Either render TLS unconditionally, or fail the template when it is disabled.
acceptance_criteria: A chart rendered with TLS disabled either fails or still produces a TLS-terminating ingress. Verified with helm template.

title: DECISION: which of Item.reorder_quantity and VendorOffer.units_per_order is authoritative
description:
Flagged while designing 0011 and deliberately not resolved there.

Item.reorder_quantity and VendorOffer.units_per_order already overlap and it is unclear which is authoritative or what unit each is expressed in. If a vendor sells zip ties 100 to a bag and units_per_order is 100, does a reorder_quantity of 2 mean two bags or two ties? The sheet stores one 'units per order' value as the string '100 ft', which is where the confusion comes from.

Adding Label.quantity does not make this worse - it describes how stock is HANDLED, not how it is bought or reordered - but it does add a third quantity-ish field and makes the ambiguity harder to keep ignoring. The low-stock alerting volunteers asked for depends on getting this right.
acceptance_criteria: It is written down which field is authoritative for reorder decisions and in what unit each is expressed; docs/data-model.md says so; an ADR records it if the answer is not obvious from the field names.

title: Deep-link entry point: /S/{code} opens the app with the code in hand
description:
Decision 0011 sections 4 and 5. Labels encode a URL, so a phone's built-in camera app - which is how volunteers scan today - deep-links into the app instead of showing a meaningless token.

An item code adds a cart line. A LOCATION code (the QR posted on the mesh room wall, the mockup's 'only 1 QR code to scan') opens the app with that location already selected as the cart's source or destination, which is how the wall code stops being a bookmark and starts answering 'where is this stock moving from?'.

nginx already serves index.html for unknown paths, but that try_files rule is now load-bearing rather than incidental.
acceptance_criteria: Opening /S/<item-code> lands in the app with that item in the cart; /S/<location-code> sets the cart location; an unknown code lands on the item search rather than an error page.

title: Label code minting and the printable label generator
description:
Decision 0011 sections 5 and 7. 'Half the QR codes don't scan' is a printing failure and no library choice fixes it.

Mint codes from Crockford Base32 (digits and uppercase letters excluding I, L, O, U), 10 characters. Encode the payload uppercase - HTTPS://INVENTORY.NYCMESH.NET/S/7QK3M2XV9A - so the encoder can use QR alphanumeric mode, which packs two characters per 11 bits instead of 8 bits each.

Generated labels must carry: error correction level Q (not the L or M most generators default to), a specified minimum module size and quiet zone, the code in human-readable text underneath so a dead QR is still a working label, and the print date so an aged batch can be replaced as a set.

Confirm the ECC percentage and the resulting QR version against ISO/IEC 18004 - the ADR's figures come from secondary sources.
acceptance_criteria: Codes mint from the stated alphabet and are unique; a printable sheet renders at ECC Q with human-readable code and print date; label revoke-and-reprint works without touching item identity.

title: Fail CI when models and migrations disagree
description:
Raised by the xhigh code review of the data-model work. CI runs lint, format, type check and tests, but nothing runs 'makemigrations --check --dry-run'. A model change committed without its migration passes CI unless a test happens to exercise the drifted field, and then fails at deploy time when migrate runs against a real database.

This matters more than usual here: the data model landed ~800 lines of migrations including hand-written RunSQL for the balance view and the append-only triggers.
acceptance_criteria: CI fails when a model change has no accompanying migration. Verified by removing a migration locally and seeing the check fail.
notes: Corrected during /simplify: the check was initially added as a CI-only step, which breaks the repo's local-equals-CI principle (ADR 0007, and the same principle ADR 0010 relies on for the schema gate). It is now backend/src/inventory/tests/test_migrations.py, so 'uv run pytest' catches drift locally and CI needs no special step. Verified failing and passing.
close_reason: Added a 'Migrations match the models' step to the backend CI job running makemigrations --check --dry-run. Verified both directions by adding a field with no migration (exit 1, CI would fail) and reverting (exit 0). Noted in the django-backend skill next to the existing migration guidance.

title: Migrate data from the Google Sheets inventory
description:
Import the existing Google Forms/Sheets inventory. Measured from the actual export, NOT the 15k+ originally assumed: 52 catalogued items and 3,439 usable submissions (Jul 2022 - Aug 2026).

Real work is data cleaning, not volume. See docs/data-model.md#migrating-the-existing-sheet:
- 145 distinct item strings map to 52 items; 41 match nothing today, 52 are retired NYCM-XX-XXXXX codes. Each becomes an ItemIdentifier row.
- 102 name spellings across 65 emails; 45% of rows have no email.
- ~18.7% of rows are corrections, not volunteer activity, and must import as adjustments.
- Locations must be extracted from the free-text notes field.
- Keep each raw source row as JSONB for provenance so the import is re-runnable.

django-import-export is likely overkill here; a management command is probably enough.
notes: Packaging ambiguity found while designing 0011: many items are counted individually but handled in packets, and historical quantities are recorded in BOTH units by different volunteers. Zip Ties Reusable (stock 600, packs of 100) shows 1 x30, 100 x17, 200 x9, 2 x5, 400 x2, 5 x2 - so a recorded '1' is either one tie or one packet and only a volunteer who was there can say which. The migration must not guess a multiplier: import the value literally and flag the item for a physical count. See decision 0011 section 6 and its Questions for the project owner #3.

title: Add LICENSE
description: MeshDB carries a LICENSE file. Pick a license consistent with NYC Mesh practice and add it before the repo goes public.
close_reason: MIT LICENSE added at the repository root. Verified the body matches the SPDX MIT text exactly after whitespace/case normalisation, which is what GitHub's licensee uses to report the license on the repo main page, and confirmed the file is not gitignored. License also declared as an SPDX expression in backend/pyproject.toml and frontend/package.json, and linked from README. Deliberately no license-files entry in pyproject: ../LICENSE sits outside the project directory and build backends reject that; the text lives once, at the root.

title: Batch validation resolves item and location one query per line
description:
StockMovementInputSerializer resolves item, from_location and to_location through PrimaryKeyRelatedField, whose to_internal_value does get(pk=...) per value. A 24-line transfer therefore costs up to 72 sequential SELECTs before a single row is written, and MAX_MOVEMENTS=500 admits up to 1500 -- against a request whose actual write is two statements. A real cart repeats the same handful of items and one or two locations, so nearly all of them are duplicates of each other.

This is the endpoint the project exists for, and it is used from a phone whose connectivity where stock is kept is unmeasured (ADR 0011 context), so latency here is worth caring about.

Two shapes: resolve in bulk in StockTransactionCreateSerializer.validate (collect every item and location id across the lines, two filter(pk__in=...) queries, report unknown ids by index through the existing error envelope, build movements with item_id=/from_location_id=); or a smaller PrimaryKeyRelatedField subclass memoising lookups across the batch, which collapses 3N to one per distinct id for much less change.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-hgm; not done there because it restructures validation and its error reporting.
acceptance_criteria: Posting a batch of N lines over M distinct items and locations issues a number of validation queries proportional to M, not N. Unknown ids are still reported by line index. Existing endpoint tests pass unchanged.

title: No database counterpart for the kind-to-required-sides rule
description:
POST /api/stock/transactions answers 409 when a batch's kind disagrees with its movements: a checkout needs a from_location on every line, a receipt a to_location, a transfer both (ADR 0011 section 6). That rule lives only in KIND_REQUIRES in views.py.

Every other per-line rule the serializer reports mirrors a real CheckConstraint (stock_movement_quantity_positive, _has_a_side, _from_differs_from_to), which is the architecture serializers.py states: the database enforces, the API reports. This one mirrors nothing, so the admin, a fixture load, or the planned sheet importer can write a checkout whose movements come from nowhere, and the 409 the client relies on is unreachable for them.

Being cross-table (StockMovement rows against their StockTransaction's kind) it needs a trigger rather than a CheckConstraint, which is why it ended up in the view. Raised while implementing inventory-tng-hgm.
acceptance_criteria: Either a trigger enforces the rule for every writer with a migration and tests, or a decision records why the rule is a client contract rather than a ledger invariant and serializers.py stops implying otherwise.

title: Should Label.quantity be NULL on a location label rather than pinned to 1
description:
ADR 0011 section 5 chose to pin Label.quantity to 1 on a location label 'rather than left to mean nothing', citing location_held_by_iff_custody as the pattern it follows. But that constraint resolves the same problem the other way: held_by is NULL when the column does not apply, not a sentinel value.

Cost of the pin: every location-label row stores a number that reads as a real multiplier. GET /api/labels/{code} returns quantity for both label kinds, and the packaging chips derive from 'the distinct quantities on an item's active labels', so each consumer must know out-of-band that 1 means 'not applicable' when the label names a location.

The alternative shape: quantity nullable, with an iff-presence constraint (quantity IS NOT NULL exactly when item IS NOT NULL) plus quantity IS NULL OR quantity > 0. A wall code then serialises as null and no client needs the convention.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-twf. Not acted on because it amends a decision record rather than an implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Either ADR 0011 section 5 is amended and the model follows, or the bead is closed recording why the sentinel is preferred.

title: Skill files restate DEVELOPERS.md instead of linking to it
description:
Found by the /simplify reuse pass. Pre-existing, not introduced by the QR work, so deliberately left out of that commit to keep it reviewable.

Both .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md declare they cover 'only conventions you cannot infer from those', then restate DEVELOPERS.md:
- react-frontend: the TypeScript typing policy (noExplicitAny / noNonNullAssertion) duplicates DEVELOPERS.md#code-style.
- django-backend: the @extend_schema rule duplicates DEVELOPERS.md#the-api-schema.
- Both Tests sections duplicate the DEVELOPERS.md#testing-and-coverage table almost line for line.

Per CLAUDE.md rule 1 the skills should keep only what is genuinely not inferable (e.g. the query-by-role rule, the manage.py path) and link for the rest.

Also noted: the 'no API URL baked into the bundle' explanation exists in three files (architecture.md, deployment.md, react-frontend skill); architecture.md should own it.
acceptance_criteria: Each duplicated topic has one owning document; the skills link rather than restate.

title: Offline queue: replay a failed batch when the network returns
description:
Deliberately deferred out of the first release by decision 0011 section 12, not dropped. The two things that would have made it a rewrite - the client-side cart and the idempotency key - are being built now, so this is purely additive.

A service worker queues a failed batch and replays it when connectivity returns. Until then, retry-on-next-open covers most of the value and needs no browser API whose support has to be checked.
acceptance_criteria: A batch submitted with the network down is recorded exactly once when it returns; the queue survives a browser restart.

title: Revisit ty once it reaches 1.0
description: ty is pre-1.0 (0.0.72) and moving quickly. It currently type checks the backend cleanly including Django/DRF stubs. Re-evaluate at 1.0; mypy remains a drop-in fallback since the stub packages are already present and only the command in DEVELOPERS.md and CI would change. See docs/decisions/0004-python-tooling.md.
notes:
Concrete gaps to re-check at 1.0, all from implementing the catalogue models (inventory-tng-1p6):
- Reverse accessors (item.identifiers, volunteer.merged_from) report unresolved-attribute.
- django-simple-history managers (item.history) likewise.
- get_FOO_display() is invisible; we write Kind(self.kind).label instead.
All are django-stubs mypy-plugin features that ty does not run. Current workaround is documented in DEVELOPERS.md#typing. When ty gains plugin support, delete the '# ty: ignore[unresolved-attribute]' comments in backend/src/inventory/tests/test_models.py and re-check.

title: Plan Django 6.1 -> 6.2 LTS upgrade before April 2027
description: Django 6.1 is a regular release with roughly a 16-month support window (chosen over 5.2 LTS deliberately). Django 6.2 is expected to be the next LTS in April 2027; schedule the upgrade rather than discovering it at EOL.
